lemmas.statement: The displayed gradient shears have subtraction inverses and preserve the standard symplectic form by symmetric Hessian blocks.
The full 2r-row gradient ledger has exactly two competitive rows and yields A, B, and C=B*A from literal exponent supports.
On the cone with sigma=sum_{i=2}^r x_i, the first and second selectors are strict, including h=2m+4 and approach to the open height face.
The seed lies strictly in the cone, and the middle lower walls, last lower wall, and height wall all map strictly inward.
C-I>0, A*1>1, and nonnegative nonzero A rows dominate every carried p and q coordinate phase by phase.
Strict uniqueness and the integral-domain highest-homogeneous-form rule prevent cancellation of every selected leading form.
C-A>0 and the last-row difference bounds make q_r strictly maximal for n>=1 and prove deg(F^n)=e_r^T*C^n*1 for n>=0 with a tied n=0 case.
Positivity of C and visibility of the seed and e_r observable give lambda_1(F)=rho(C).
U has dimension r-3, A and B act as -I on U, C acts as I, and the equal-middle complement E yields a direct invariant decomposition.
The declared common-middle coordinate convention yields the displayed Q, its trace, principal-minor sum, determinant, cubic factor, and P(1).
The seed lies in E, so the exact degree sequence has the displayed cubic annihilator, while P(1) gives exact unit multiplicity r-3.
The g=2r seed tie, r=3 predecessor reduction, and four-nonzero-coefficient domain argument establish only their precisely bounded boundary and corollary claims.
